definition: A change of state of a gas at constant volume, so the gas does no work and all the heat supplied changes its internal energy ($Q = \Delta U$).
A change of state of a gas at constant pressure, in which the work done by the gas is $W = P\Delta V$.
A change of state of a gas at constant temperature; for an ideal gas the internal energy does not change, so the heat supplied equals the work done by the gas ($Q = W$).
A change of state with no thermal energy transferred to or from the gas ($Q = 0$), so $\Delta U = -W$; for a monatomic ideal gas, $PV^{\frac{5}{3}}$ stays constant.
A graph of the pressure of a gas against its volume, on which each point is a state; the area under a line is the work done by the gas, and the area enclosed by a cycle is the net work.
A device that takes a gas round a repeating cycle, taking in thermal energy from a hot reservoir, doing useful work and giving out the rest as thermal energy to a cold reservoir.

A theoretical reversible cycle of two isothermal and two adiabatic stages, whose efficiency $1 - \frac{T_\text{c}}{T_\text{h}}$ (temperatures in kelvin) is the maximum for any heat engine between those reservoirs.
